expect.note: `_nearest`'s `loose` switch is keyword-only with no default, so a caller that forgets it fails loudly instead of restoring the ungated rung 3

provenance: PR #42 R18, promoted out of debt by the human's explicit ask ('fix rung 3 too'). The R7 repair routed every M38 narrowing rung through one flag, `may_narrow` — except that rung 3 reads it through a parameter, `_nearest(..., loose=)`, which shipped as `loose: bool = True`. Both call sites passed it correctly, so nothing was wrong; what was wrong is the shape. R7's defect WAS a narrowing path nobody remembered to gate, and a permissive default reproduces it for the next caller by omission, silently, with no case able to go red — the two R7 cases exercise the real path and never see a default. `loose` is now keyword-only with no default: a caller that forgets it raises TypeError. Watched red first by restoring `loose: bool = True` and running this case: `passed false`, `loose {'kind': 'POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD', 'default': 'True'}`.

triage.what_this_grades: the guard on the guard: pure code inspection, no browser, no page. It reads the signature rather than calling the function, because the failure it grades is a call site that does not exist yet.
triage.not_covered: a future caller that passes `loose=True` deliberately where it should pass the flag. That is a decision, not an omission, and it is visible in the diff — this case only makes the omission impossible.
triage.why_not_invariant: it belongs in the `invariant` suite by shape and is tagged `fast` only, deliberately. Adding it makes that suite 59 cases, and the committed ledger already holds a 59-case invariant row from 2026-08-16 (32.25s, an unrelated older tree at the same count). `published-band-matches-the-ledger` filters by exact case count, so item 3 (same-ceiling) would compare a ~13.5s band against that row's 40s ceiling and go red — T-R50's declared defect, not this milestone's, and the only ways out are publishing a false band or deleting a real gate run. It runs in `fast`, which is the gate that blocks a commit, and moves to `invariant` when T-R50 is fixed.
